steps.title: Obtain Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD)
steps.explanation: Procure Form 4 (for institutional deaths) or Form 4A (for domiciliary/home deaths) from the attending doctor or medical institution.
steps.why_now: The Registrar requires a formalized medical cause of death to officially record the event in the Civil Registration System.
steps.where: Attending Hospital or Registered Medical Practitioner

steps.title: Register Death with Local Registrar
steps.explanation: Submit the application for death registration to the concerned Panchayat, Municipality, or Corporation within 21 days of the occurrence to avoid late fees.
steps.why_now: Legally required under the Registration of Births & Deaths Act, 1969. It is the prerequisite for generating a valid Death Certificate.
documents: Proof of birth of deceased (Birth certificate/SSLC)
Affidavit specifying date and time of death
steps.fee: Nil if within 21 days; Rs. 2 to Rs. 10 for delayed registration

steps.title: Download Official Death Certificate
steps.explanation: Once registered, use the citizen portal (Sevana/K-SMART) to search and download the digitally signed Death Certificate.
steps.why_now: Provides legal proof needed to settle insurance, bank accounts, and property inheritance.
steps.where: K-SMART Portal (Local Self Government Department, Kerala)
steps.fee: Rs. 5 per extract (or to be verified)
